project.title: Unified Business Intelligence
project.shortDescription: Reconciled 2026-10-28: merged delivery separated from live verification; remaining issues name blockers and next steps.
project.readme:
# Unified Business Intelligence — reconciled delivery board

Reviewed 2026-10-28 (America/Cancun) against all 110 existing cards, issue handoffs, current open PRs and recent merged PRs across CrawlSEO, Site-Agent, HelloAda and Wix Bridge. 16 completed PR/historical cards are archived with their links/history preserved. A new verification follow-up captures the partial AEO pilot.

## What the board means
- Merged: implementation or evidence delivered. It does not prove live integration, human acceptance or customer publication. Readiness is cleared on terminal cards.
- In review: a concrete review is pending. Site-Agent #386 has failing PR #388 and missing browser evidence; CrawlSEO #49 awaits owner relevance judgment.
- Ready: a specified, unclaimed next task. Requires a fresh valid claim and bounded draft PR before implementation.
- Specified + Needs review: remaining scope/contract must be reviewed before pickup.
- Specified + Blocked by dependencies: operational prerequisite or verification evidence is missing; the owning issue names the next actor.
- Deferred: intentionally unscheduled capability. Webflow #25 stays deferred.
- No card is marked In progress from an old claim alone. No Verified status was inferred from a merge.

## Next work
1. Site-Agent #421 (P0): prevent missing runtime extras from passing the release gate; verify rollback health.
2. Site-Agent #379: failed-builder budget accounting; #410: diagnose SIGINT and record authoritative timeout/signal stages.
3. Site-Agent #386 / PR #388: failing checks plus real desktop/mobile upload and dialog proof.
4. Site-Agent #428: remaining candidate/deployed shared-runtime parity; manifest and lockfile fixes already merged.
5. HelloAda #19: keywordResearch + CrawlSEO site identity contract, then the existing panel card/deep link. Existing panel is delivered.
6. Live gates: Site-Agent #352 (incubation/research/context), #353 (disposable site), #354 (Google provisioning); Wix Bridge #11 is credential/target-blocked. Human gates #355 and Wix #12 wait for their producer evidence. CrawlSEO #49 is the owner relevance verdict.
7. AEO pilot follow-up: https://github.com/weareheadless/crawlseo/issues/127 — Google baseline exists; Perplexity, per-question failure attribution and authenticated production UI proof remain.
8. Site-Agent #252 / draft PR #253: incomplete exact maintenance preview/review path; public maintenance test does not prove private candidate review. Keep the existing review boundaries.

Use repository + issue number as the unique task identity: UI/OPS numbers repeat across repositories. Missing Work ID fields have been filled without renumbering historical tasks.

## Source and operating rules
Canonical design: https://github.com/weareheadless/crawlseo/tree/main/docs/architecture/centralized-intelligence
Issue bodies and direct prerequisites define scope; Project fields summarize it. Current claims, exact PR diff, CI, tests and release/verification receipts supply evidence. Historical planning READMEs are not live dispatch instructions.

Use the existing shared coordinator and repository AGENTS instructions. Update issue state, claim handoff and Project status together when a bounded change merges; keep unmet acceptance in an explicitly scoped open issue. Attach exact evidence and the next actor to every blocked/review item. Do not repeat stale status comments or launch workers without a current task/run.

This board does not run an unattended orchestrator or authorize provider spend, customer publication or production deployment. Existing exact approval and release paths remain binding. Private repository access is required.

fields.Title: Unify maintenance authoring with exact canonical design review in Payload

content.title: Unify maintenance authoring with exact canonical design review in Payload
content.body:
## Proven failure and scope

Acceptance testing for #243/#246 found a disconnected source-review lane. Oceanic job64 correctly authored candidate `504f2ca41ec93f7e9e66c9d0cf9560db30b008e4`, pending draft61, one CSS rule in the planned file. Source scope is fixed (#251 deployed); production remains at `814dd597633c5daa65e4279259df7bcc5c5318e5`. Do not call this a reviewed/ready website change.

`WebsiteWorkspace.previewUrl` always targets ordinary Payload preview. `loadPreviewPlan` can clear requires_build without selecting the candidate runtime. CSS source is marked ready by an overlay classifier, but Payload admin never applies that overlay. There are no corresponding source review decisions in this window. The bridge also restricts source preview job IDs to digits while the job service uses UUIDs, and GET latest is not mapped.

Read-only architectural reviews found deeper gaps: SourceDeploymentService's raw runtime proxy has no demonstrated Next mount/basePath contract; effect receipt hashes are not a complete frozen Payload/media snapshot; source approval can trust saved readiness rather than exact current review evidence. The canonical design-run lifecycle already owns candidate/validation/review identities, but currently lacks a maintenance intent and its actual dynamic Next/Payload rendering suitability must be proven rather than assumed.

This is a meaningful pipeline unification, not a missing-button patch. Implementation requires owner direction; investigation and gates are recorded here. Do not introduce another runtime/snapshot/approval architecture in the meantime.

## Target

One owner journey: request -> Ada's task plan -> focused implementation -> exact candidate build/render -> review in the existing Payload website window -> explicit approve/revise/decline -> canonical release. Retain tenant frontend autonomy and shared Payload/schema authority. Reuse existing chat jobs, design-run lifecycle, evidence, API, approval records and production release queue. Retire the old spawn_build/stage_merge/CSS-overlay owner lane only after verified parity. Never restore the standalone legacy admin, infer content from JSX, or use fake intake/design parents to fit maintenance into initial-site creation.

## Implementation sequence

1. Establish the single exact Next/Payload render contract first. Bind deployed tenant source SHA AND shared-runtime fingerprint, candidate SHA, affected routes, canonical Payload document/global revision set, locale and referenced media to one immutable review identity. Inspect existing snapshot/build services and reuse them where actually suitable. Do not assume configured current_content or a receipt hash supplies the entire render dependencies. Missing required data is an explicit failure.
2. Provide mount-aware candidate rendering for the actual Next/Payload application: HTML, hydration, chunks, CSS/fonts/images, navigation and relevant requests must stay within the candidate, not leak to live /_next or silently show the live site. Prefer framework build-time mount configuration over HTML-string patches. Define browser isolation before running candidate JavaScript; the same website window must not imply access to authenticated admin APIs. Keep production credentials out of candidate builds/browser code.
3. Add an explicit typed maintenance operation to the canonical request/run lifecycle. Use verified existing production base, owner request, task scope, affected route and relevant frozen business/content evidence. Do not stage initial-site content or reopen creative direction. Preserve exact-file native OpenCode permissions within the common frontend ownership boundary; do not replace them with the whole frontend allowlist or prompt-only restrictions. Design intake retains its confirmed experience requirements.
4. Produce one durable candidate build/validation/review receipt tied to that identity. Persist real progress and terminal failures; no CSS-only ready shortcut. A candidate is reviewable only when the exact artifact/render evidence exists. Restoration after reconnect uses exact run/draft/candidate identity, not branch-latest inference or silent automatic rebuilds.
5. Connect that receipt to the existing Payload website pane with clear preparing/blocked/ready states. Provide one source-change decision bar, separate from native Payload document publishing, without another dashboard. The chat must state the actual readiness and how to review; it must never claim that a static content preview is the new code candidate.
6. Reuse approval API and durable records, NOT the old weak readiness semantics. Source approval must require the immutable review identity and exact expected candidate/base/runtime/content identities. Reject stale/dead/wrong/missing review evidence and concurrent branch movement. Ensure the actual merge/promotion operation receives atomic expected-SHA constraints; checking a branch and then merging a moving branch is insufficient. No automatic publication. Repeated approval retains one release identity.
7. Retire the disconnected spawn_build/stage_merge/CSS-overlay owner path after parity. Handle its pending records explicitly as incomplete/nonapprovable; do not reinterpret old ready flags as new evidence or fabricate receipts. No generic fallback, tenant exception or duplicate schema/content store.
8. Commit/test/publish any shared package, pin exact assets, release API and shared Worker runtime through the canonical VPS queues. Canary and fanout remain automatic; do not manually deploy or edit tenant repositories for common code.

## Acceptance

- Real maintenance request from Payload reaches Ada, the scoped implementation agent, exact candidate build and owner-visible review; change is visible and keyboard/filter behavior works. Production remains unchanged until explicit approval.
- Correct candidate assets, hydration and navigation at actual review mount; no asset requests accidentally use live /_next. Missing content/media fails clearly; frozen revisions remain stable despite later content edits.
- Authenticated UUID preview/decision round trips work; unauthenticated/cross-tenant access fails; candidate JavaScript cannot use the owner's privileged admin session.
- Stale review hash, moved base/head, wrong run/draft/job/content/runtime identity, missing/dead artifact, failed build and concurrent branch movement reject approval; repeated approval is idempotent.
- Initial intake/design constraints, shared schema/field bindings, existing approved tenant composition and canonical release gates remain intact.
- Fresh authenticated browser evidence beside exact receipts. Passing unit tests, a model claim, saved ready flag or healthy Worker alone is not completion.

Related: #243 (source scope fixed/closed), #244/#245 (durable outcomes/status fixed), #246 (focused agent implementation deployed, owner journey incomplete).

- [ ] Task metadata records issue/work ID, actual agent run, branch, baseline, contract and allowed paths.
- [ ] Conflicting claims, duplicate task PRs, stale metadata, unfilled handoffs and out-of-scope renames fail checks.
- [ ] Manager check reads real Project readiness/dependencies and current-head CI; Deferred work cannot auto-start.
- [ ] Board sync never marks Verified or promotes Deferred work.
- [ ] Shared key is reused; no personal key is added to CI. Workflow-token permissions are bounded and checker code is pinned.
- [ ] Agent instructions explain pickup, replanning, latest-diff review, and stopping before merge/deploy.
- [ ] Merge-protection availability/adoption limits are reported honestly; no nonexistent required check blocks bootstrap.

## Validation
Meaningful Node tests for the new coordination behavior; live read-only Project query; validate workflow wiring and scoped consumer diffs. Application and platform publication rules remain unchanged. Shared credentials cannot guarantee independent identity; the workflow enforces cooperative task discipline and test/review evidence, not a new security boundary.

## Implementation and current handoff

- Shared coordinator: https://github.com/weareheadless/site-agent/pull/342
- CrawlSEO consumer: https://github.com/weareheadless/crawlseo/pull/28
- Wix Bridge consumer: https://github.com/weareheadless/wix-site-bridge/pull/7
- HelloAda consumer: https://github.com/weareheadless/helloada/pull/12
- Pinned shared implementation: `21f1bc35e1fd9ebb537667489ce41d5370cdc13a`.

21 coordinator tests pass locally and the coordinator step passes in GitHub CI. Actual shared-key claim and live Project reads succeeded; the manager check correctly reports Pending while required current-head code checks are unfinished. CrawlSEO's 382 tests/typecheck, Wix Bridge's 19 tests, and current HelloAda CI pass. Site-Agent's full application suite is still running; do not describe that handoff as fully passed yet.

Ready for agents now filters `readiness:Ready status:Ready`, excluding already-claimed tasks. Existing Source/HelloAda CI is reused; no personal key or Project secret is added to CI. The metadata workflow uses GitHub's built-in token and pinned checker code, not task-branch execution. Code tests run separately. No new identity/assignment service, scheduled dispatcher or automatic merger.

Adoption: review/merge the shared implementation, then the thin consumers. Automatic defaults become active after merge. Required branch protections remain unchanged during bootstrap; do not report CI feedback as an already-enforced GitHub merge rule. With a shared key/account, manager latest-diff review is the decision gate, not independent authenticated authorship. Customer publication/production release remains separate.

fields.Title: [OPS-002] Add the bounded generic Wix prepared-embed capability needed by UI-014

content.title: [OPS-002] Add the bounded generic Wix prepared-embed capability needed by UI-014
content.body:
Supporting producer task for [UI-014](https://github.com/weareheadless/crawlseo/issues/24), within the approved shared-intelligence execution plan. Existing inventory UI-013 proved the producer gap; this is not a new publishing service or a customer-site task.

## Bounded result

Extend the generic bridge once, using its existing manifest allowlist, official Custom Embeds client, private state/snapshot/receipt helpers. Expose a versioned capability declaration from inspect and a narrowly prepared, manifest-scoped HTML embed plan/apply/reconcile operation. Do not upstream arbitrary host CLI behavior or claim code/CMS/Editor/SEO publication support.

Reviewed producer baseline: `bac2779e87c9616804758680cf121669f3c5a40a`; inventory commit `74ef4104e267ec712f32c7a7d9082287b45de39d`. Shared contract pin for coordination: CrawlSEO `d939bd0d930960dba9b05a3b97b218d0a0a94fa7`.

## Acceptance

- Inspect reports a stable contract/version and only implemented capabilities; unsupported operations remain false and no intelligence binding is activated.
- A private prepared candidate binds exact alias/site/snippet, existing placement/page scope/category/load-once, current revision/content hash, desired content hash and plan identity. Public output never exposes prepared HTML, tokens or private snapshot contents.
- Apply requires the exact reviewed plan/hash and explicit apply flag; re-reads scope/revision/hash, rejects stale or changed input, writes durable intent before the official-API mutation, and records outcome/readback afterwards.
- Concurrent/repeated apply cannot produce duplicate writes. Unknown/lost responses remain blocked until exact readback reconciliation; never infer missing receipt means no effect or auto-retry an uncertain write.
- Reconcile is read-only, checks the same exact target and expected desired hash/scope, and preserves uncertainty for unresolved or conflicting state.
- Existing CLI/MCP/manifest behavior and interactive code publishing are preserved. No private editor endpoint, arbitrary CMS write, customer repository or new credential/service is introduced.
- Fake-client tests cover valid plan/apply, CAS conflicts, scope drift, different plan/hash, concurrency, loss after mutation, receipt persistence interruption, repeated/restart readback, unsupported capabilities and redaction. Existing npm test passes.

## Implementation paths and handoff

Start with src/bridge.mjs, cli.mjs, mcp.mjs, release.mjs, security.mjs and existing wix-client.mjs; a small prepared-embed module is acceptable. Keep existing methods and local private-state conventions. Tests live in test/; update the compatibility fixture/docs so CrawlSEO can consume the exact protocol. First report exact scope for PM claim, then Luna light authors all implementation/revisions. Open a draft PR with task JSON and actual tested SHA. Root independently reviews/tests/merges.

No live Wix request, customer selection, snippet apply, publish or binding activation is authorized by this engineering issue. UI-014's separately authorized disposable pilot remains a parent completion gate. This producer is a supporting subtask; it does not replace or close UI-014.

fields.Title: [UI-019] Serve bounded prelaunch research for domainless incubation projects

content.title: [UI-019] Serve bounded prelaunch research for domainless incubation projects
content.body:
Producer gap discovered while implementing site-agent UI-006.

**Gap.** Incubation projects are registered through `POST /api/projects/register` (UI-002), which creates a workspace and project and no site or domain. The only bounded research contract is `seo_request_research_report`, which requires a `Site` with a domain: `requestResearchReport` resolves `site.domain` for `taskDefinitions` and persists `ResearchRun.siteId`. So an in-incubation (pre-domain) project has no way to request bounded research today.

**Consequence.** HelloAda cannot route incubation research into CrawlSEO before a domain exists. That is the first half of the product goal, so it is blocking rather than deferred.

**Bounded result.** A project-scoped, domainless prelaunch research request that:
- creates one bounded research run for (projectId, idempotencyKey, period) without requiring a site or domain;
- runs only provider work that is meaningful without a site domain (keyword seeds, market/news/web observations), and reports the domain-dependent tasks as explicitly skipped rather than guessed;
- returns immutable findings with provider/source identity, content hash and retrieval date, reusing the UI-005 source identity so a second request never re-dispatches the same fresh source;
- keeps the existing paid-budget contract: a configured USD ceiling or the request is rejected, actual cost settled, and no dispatch when the ceiling is absent;
- exposes status/report reads and honest partial/blocked states.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] A domainless project can create one bounded run and read immutable findings; a repeated idempotency key returns the same run and spends nothing.
- [ ] No fake site, placeholder domain or synthesized crawl is created to satisfy the research path.
- [ ] Domain-dependent tasks are reported as skipped with a reason, never fabricated.
- [ ] Reuse respects the UI-005 project/provider/URL identity and freshness rules; no cross-project leak.
- [ ] Budget absent/invalid fails closed; actual provider cost is settled for every task.
- [ ] Provider outage returns partial/blocked, never invented retrieval dates.

**Consumer.** site-agent UI-006 (`src/site_agent/application/incubation_research.py`) will consume this instead of local feed dispatch.

No new broker, vector store, provider framework or cross-tenant cache. Paid dispatch at prelaunch requires explicit owner authorization per project; owner has authorized a few-cents-per-project-per-month envelope for incubation research.

fields.Title: [UI-020] Wire question coverage into the editorial flow

content.title: [UI-020] Wire question coverage into the editorial flow
content.body:
Follow-up split from UI-007 (#19) so the design/launch chain is not blocked.

**What exists.** The evidence-linked, hash-bound question-coverage record is merged: `recordQuestionCoverage` takes explicit finding, knowledge document/field/revision and section/content-hash identity, validates provenance and publication use, and records `covered` or `unresolved` (with the missing-evidence request).

**Gap.** Nothing calls it. No current path supplies both the canonical business-knowledge field/revision and the exact section content hash at the moment content is drafted or reviewed.

**Bounded result.** Wire the one real caller: when editorial review accepts a section, record coverage with the exact section hash and the specific knowledge field/revision that answers the question; when it cannot, record `unresolved` with the missing evidence.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] Accepting a section records `covered` with that section's exact hash and a resolvable knowledge field/revision.
- [ ] A question with no usable evidence records `unresolved` with a request, never a generated claim.
- [ ] Re-reviewing unchanged content does not duplicate rows; changed content invalidates prior coverage.
- [ ] No fabricated facts, no URL/title-only matching.

No new store, workflow or provider. Reuse the merged coverage record and the existing editorial review path.

fields.Title: [UI-021] Ingest observed AI visibility evidence for the supported provider

content.title: [UI-021] Ingest observed AI visibility evidence for the supported provider
content.body:
Follow-up split from UI-010 (#22) so the citation-gap chain is not blocked by ingestion work.

**What exists.** The versioned provider capability matrix and the access-signal rule: robots, sitemap, bot user-agent or HTTP 200 are access evidence only and can never imply ingestion, citation, mention, ranking or coverage. Unobserved surfaces report unknown with a reason.

**Bounded result.** For one supported provider, ingest genuinely observed visibility evidence through an explicit, auditable path (provider export/API or an operator-labelled manual import), store it as labelled observations with source kind, provider/model, timestamp, question set and explicit uncertainty, and keep mentions, recommendations and citations separate.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] Only observed evidence is ingested; nothing is simulated, inferred from access signals, or backfilled.
- [ ] Every observation carries source kind, provider, timestamp, question-set version and the denominator/coverage it came from.
- [ ] Unavailable or partial evidence stays explicitly unknown/partial rather than zero.
- [ ] Repeated ingestion does not duplicate; a changed observation is versioned, not overwritten.
- [ ] No paid provider dispatch without an existing budget ceiling.

No new provider framework, broker or cross-tenant cache.

fields.Title: [OPS-003] Live paid prelaunch research, and replay spends nothing

content.title: [OPS-003] Live paid prelaunch research, and replay spends nothing
content.body:
Work ID **OPS-003**. Verification, not implementation.

Exercise the merged prelaunch research path against production CrawlSEO with a real provider call, on `ada-provision-test` (or a new internal test project you create and remove), never a customer project.

Steps:
1. Budget for the test project (fixed, do not exceed): monthly allowance **USD 1.00**, per-operation ceiling **USD 0.10**. State both in the evidence.
2. Request one prelaunch research run through `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/prelaunch-research` with a real service credential and a brief built from a small real business (a throwaway test profile).
3. Wait for the run to complete; record the provider task receipts, the actual settled cost, the task count and the skip reasons for domain-dependent tasks.
4. Replay the identical request: assert the same run is returned, no new tasks, no new reservations, no additional provider operations.
5. Read back findings, sources and the canonical knowledge document shape.

Evidence: request/response bodies (secrets redacted), the run's task rows, reservation/settlement rows, and the actual charge. Then state the total spend.

Do not touch a customer project or budget. Do not raise the ceiling mid-run.

## Rules for every verification issue

- Exercise the real production path. Fixtures are not evidence.
- Use a **low-impact target**: a subpage, a test tenant, or `ada-provision-test`. Never the homepage, never a live customer page, never a customer project's budget.
- Cap any paid work explicitly and state the cap in the evidence.
- Record what you did, the exact command or API call, the response, and the observable result. If something cannot be exercised, say so with the missing prerequisite instead of approximating.
- Leave the system in its prior state: remove test projects/tenants/pages you created, or state exactly what remains and why.
- Do not declare success from a 200, a log line, or a code path. Success means the user-visible effect is observable.

fields.Title: [UI-023] Give AEO and GEO a real surface in CrawlSEO

content.title: [UI-023] Give AEO and GEO a real surface in CrawlSEO
content.body:
The intelligence chain is merged and deployed, but an owner cannot see any of it. There is no AI-visibility page, no place showing which questions are answered, and no view of what the visibility importer stored. Backend without a surface is not a product.

Build one site-scoped **Intelligence** area (new route group under the existing site navigation) with four sections:

1. **AI access readiness** — from the capability matrix plus the crawl audit: can AI crawlers reach the site (robots/sitemap/HTTP), and what is *unknown*. Access evidence is never presented as visibility.
2. **Visibility observed** — imported observations grouped by provider and model surface, each with question-set version, observed date, denominator and the mention/recommendation/citation split. Unobserved engines render as **unknown**, never as zero or "not cited".
3. **Questions** — question coverage: covered (with the knowledge field/revision and section hash that answers it) versus unresolved with the missing-evidence request and its linked Action.
4. **Sources** — the research sources behind the findings, with provider, retrieval date and reuse state.

Rules:
- Every number carries its provenance and its uncertainty. No invented denominators, no "0 citations" when nothing was observed.
- Empty states explain what would populate them and how, instead of showing a blank panel.
- Reuse the existing data access paths and components; no new store, no duplicate query layer.
- Server-rendered, no client fetch waterfalls; works at 390px.

Acceptance: an owner opening a site with no imports sees a truthful "nothing observed yet" state with the next step; with one import sees the observations and the unknown engines; the questions list links each covered item to its evidence and each unresolved item to its Action.

fields.Title: [UI-024] Make intelligence a filterable dimension and show why an Action exists

content.title: [UI-024] Make intelligence a filterable dimension and show why an Action exists
content.body:
Actions are the outcome of research, but the Work tab treats every action the same and the detail page does not show the reasoning chain. An owner cannot tell an AEO action from an SEO action, or why it exists.

1. **Dimension taxonomy**: classify every Action by dimension — `seo`, `aeo`, `geo`, `content`, `technical` — derived from its source (coverage gap → aeo; visibility gap → geo; crawl/schema issue → technical/seo; content draft → content). Store it as a derived field with a single mapping function, not scattered conditionals.
2. **Filtering**: Work tab filters by dimension and by state, with counts per filter, preserving the existing tabs. Deep-linkable (`?dimension=aeo`).
3. **Provenance chain** on the action detail page: canonical knowledge revision and field → research finding → source(s) with retrieval date → question coverage state → the Action → its outcome. Each hop links to the page that owns it. If a hop is missing, say so explicitly rather than hiding it.

Rules: no new table if the dimension can be derived deterministically; if it must be stored, add one additive column and backfill from the existing sources. Reuse existing components.

Acceptance: filtering to AEO shows only AEO actions with a correct count; every action detail shows the full chain or names the missing hop; no action changes state or content because of this work.

fields.Title: [UI-025] Show the owner their intelligence in HelloAda

content.title: [UI-025] Show the owner their intelligence in HelloAda
content.body:
The owner works in HelloAda, but everything about their business intelligence lives in CrawlSEO. They currently see nothing there.

Add a read-only **Intelligence** summary to the owner's project view:
- the accepted business profile and when it last changed (from canonical knowledge, with revision),
- research status: last run, what it found, what is still pending or blocked,
- question coverage: how many questions are answered, how many are waiting on the owner,
- AI visibility: what has been observed and what is explicitly unknown,
- the outstanding Actions that came out of it, each linking through to the owning surface.

Rules: read through the existing service boundary; no copy of the data, no second store, no derived truth. Unknown stays unknown. If CrawlSEO is unavailable, show the state as unavailable with a reason — never an empty success.

Acceptance: an owner with no research sees a truthful empty state and the next step; an owner with research sees their profile, the findings summary, the unanswered questions, and can follow each item to its detail.

fields.Title: [OPS-010] Align the prelaunch research service scope so paid verification can run

content.title: [OPS-010] Align the prelaunch research service scope so paid verification can run
content.body:
Live verification of the paid path (OPS-003) is blocked: the available project service credential carries `seo:research:request`, while the prelaunch research endpoint requires `seo:research`, which is not in the known scope set.

Decide and implement one of:
1. add `seo:research` to the issued credential scopes for project registration, or
2. align the endpoint to require the scope the credential actually has, and update the capability/scope documentation.

Whichever is chosen, the credential a site-agent tenant receives must be able to do exactly the operations the contract says it can, no more. Update the registration contract, the scope list, and the tests that assert the granted scopes.

Acceptance: a freshly issued project credential can call the prelaunch research endpoint successfully within its budget; a credential without the scope is rejected; the documented scopes match the code.

fields.Title: [UI-026] Turn detected AEO/GEO gaps into verifiable improvement Actions

content.title: [UI-026] Turn detected AEO/GEO gaps into verifiable improvement Actions
content.body:
AEO/GEO was meant to improve visibility, not only to measure it. Today the only improvement Actions that exist come from unresolved question coverage. The crawl audit detects business-content and structured-data problems but stops at reporting them, and AI access problems (crawler blocking, missing sitemap coverage, no machine-readable summary) are not turned into work at all.

Make every detected gap produce an actionable, verifiable Action.

**Gap sources to cover**
1. Audit findings: published content or JSON-LD disagrees with canonical knowledge, or the fact is absent from the page.
2. Question coverage: a question has no sourced answer (already exists — keep it).
3. AI access: robots rules that block named AI crawlers, pages missing from the sitemap, no machine-readable site summary, missing or invalid business identity structured data.
4. Knowledge quality: facts that are assumed/deferred/disputed and block an otherwise ready answer.

**Each Action must carry its own verifier.** The Action states the change to make and the exact check that proves it worked — the same check that produced it. On the next crawl/audit that check re-runs, so the Action moves to `FULFILLED` automatically when the condition clears, and stays open while it does not. That closes the loop without needing AI-visibility measurement.

**Rules**
- Deterministic mapping only: a detected condition maps to one Action kind with one verifier. No model judgement in the detection path.
- Deduplicate by (project, gap identity) so a re-crawl never multiplies actions.
- Never assert a fact the owner has not confirmed; an Action may say "confirm this claim", not invent the claim.
- No paid dispatch, no content rewriting in this issue — detection and Action creation only.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] An audit mismatch produces exactly one Action naming the page, the field and the check.
- [ ] A robots rule blocking an AI crawler produces a technical Action with the rule quoted.
- [ ] An absent machine-readable summary produces a content Action.
- [ ] Re-crawling unchanged input creates no duplicates; a cleared condition moves the Action to `FULFILLED`.
- [ ] A still-failing condition keeps it open with the current evidence attached.

fields.Title: [OPS-011] Remove the Wix concurrency test flake

content.title: [OPS-011] Remove the Wix concurrency test flake
content.body:
Twice today a full-suite run failed in a Wix concurrency test and passed on immediate rerun (crawlseo CI on `48d3eaf`, and a local run on `901b0fa`). Under the new rule that is a defect, not a rerun.

Find the nondeterminism and remove it: shared fixture or database state between tests, real timers, parallel workers touching the same rows, or a race the test itself creates and does not await deterministically. Do not add retries, sleeps or skips.

Acceptance:
- [ ] The test fails deterministically when the behaviour is broken (prove it by reverting the guard locally and seeing the failure).
- [ ] The suite passes ten consecutive runs with no failures.
- [ ] No sleep-based synchronisation is added; where waiting is unavoidable, it waits on an observable condition with a bounded timeout.
- [ ] Any shared state is isolated per test (unique ids, per-test cleanup, no reliance on execution order).

fields.Title: [UI-027] Expose a read-only intelligence summary for the owner app

content.title: [UI-027] Expose a read-only intelligence summary for the owner app
content.body:
UI-025 (the HelloAda owner intelligence view) is blocked because there is no service boundary to read from: HelloAda only calls control-plane registration and bootstrap. The owner app must not query CrawlSEO directly or copy its data.

Expose one read-only summary from site-agent, the service that already owns the tenant and the CrawlSEO connection:

`GET /api/tenants/{tenantId}/intelligence` (authenticated with the existing owner handoff credential, tenant-scoped, no cross-tenant read) returning a single payload:
- `businessProfile`: documentId, revision, acceptedRevision, updatedAt, and the confirmed field names with their status (no unpublished internals).
- `research`: last run id, status, period, finishedAt, finding count, and `pendingReason`/`blockedReason` when not complete.
- `coverage`: counts of covered and unresolved questions plus the unresolved items with their missing-evidence text and linked action id.
- `visibility`: per provider/surface, observed count, denominator, latest observed date, and `unknown` where nothing was observed — never zero.
- `actions`: open, fulfilled and failed counts plus the most recent open items with id, title, dimension.

Rules: assemble from the canonical sources through the existing application service; store nothing; unknown stays unknown; if CrawlSEO is unavailable return an explicit `unavailable` state with a reason and a 200/503 that the caller can render honestly. No new table, no cached copy, no derived truth.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A tenant with no research returns a complete payload with explicit empty/unknown states, not nulls that read as success.
- [ ] A tenant with research returns revisions, findings count and coverage matching what CrawlSEO holds.
- [ ] An unknown surface is distinguishable from zero.
- [ ] Another tenant's data is never returned; a missing credential is 401.
- [ ] CrawlSEO outage yields an explicit unavailable state, not an empty payload.

fields.Title: [UI-028] Surface prelaunch research results and derive Actions from them

content.title: [UI-028] Surface prelaunch research results and derive Actions from them
content.body:
The paid prelaunch research path now works in production — run `cmvqm9i130001oyri2trh7hdx` completed with 5 keyword tasks for **USD 0.0624** — and it produces nothing the owner can see. No findings, no Actions, no report view. That is why "keyword research" looks like it returns no results.

**Bounded result.** Make a completed prelaunch research run legible and actionable:
1. **Report view** for a project's prelaunch run: period, task list with status and cost, the keyword results per seed (volume, difficulty, intent where the provider returned them), and the explicit skip reasons for domain-dependent tasks. Reuse the existing research-run page conventions.
2. **Derive Actions** from those results with the same discipline as the crawl gap Actions: a keyword opportunity becomes an Action with the check that proves it was addressed, deduplicated by (project, gap identity), never inventing facts. At minimum: create/refresh content for a seed with real volume and no ranking page; consolidate when two seeds target the same intent.
3. **Surface it** in the Intelligence page's Questions/Sources sections and in Work with the `aeo`/`seo` dimension, so the owner can trace run → result → Action.

Rules: no paid dispatch in this issue; read what the run stored. If the stored task payload lacks what a view needs, say so explicitly rather than inventing numbers. Unknown stays unknown.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A completed run renders its tasks, costs and results; skipped tasks state why.
- [ ] At least the two Action derivations above exist, deduplicated, with verifiers.
- [ ] The Intelligence page and Work show the run's output and link to it.
- [ ] Re-running derivation on unchanged results creates no duplicates.

fields.Title: [OPS-013] Run the worker from an immutable release and prove it after deploy

content.title: [OPS-013] Run the worker from an immutable release and prove it after deploy
content.body:
Root cause of the paid-run failure, found in production: the `crawlseo-worker` PM2 process runs from the mutable `/SEO` source checkout, not from an immutable release slot. After the UI-019 schema change, its generated Prisma client still expected `Job.siteId` to be non-nullable, so every site-less job crashed with `Error converting field "siteId" of expected non-nullable type "String", found incompatible value of "null"` and burned all 10 attempts. The web process was fine because it runs from the release slot.

I repaired production by checking `/SEO` out to the deployed SHA, `npm ci`, `npx prisma generate`, restarting the worker, and requeueing the job — which then completed and spent USD 0.0624.

**Bounded result.** Remove the class of failure:
1. The worker (and MCP) must run from an immutable source checkout matching the deployed SHA, the same way the web process runs from its release slot — or from a staged release that includes what the worker needs.
2. Deployment must fail if the worker's generated Prisma client does not match the migrated schema, instead of discovering it as a runtime crash on the first site-less job.
3. A post-deploy smoke check: enqueue one site-less job and require it to complete, or fail the release.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Worker and MCP run from a versioned checkout or slot, never from the mutable source tree.
- [ ] A schema/client mismatch fails the release, not the first job.
- [ ] A post-deploy smoke job proves the worker can process a site-less job.
- [ ] `deploy/README.md` documents the worker's release identity and the smoke check.

fields.Title: [OPS-014] Seed canonical knowledge and prove the AEO loop in production

content.title: [OPS-014] Seed canonical knowledge and prove the AEO loop in production
content.body:
No canonical business knowledge exists in production (`BusinessKnowledgeDocument` count is 0), so the audit has nothing to compare against, coverage has nothing to answer, and gap Actions cannot be produced. Every downstream AEO feature is blocked on this, not on code.

**Bounded result.** Take one real project end to end in production and leave it usable:

1. Pick `ada-provision-test` (internal test project). Confirm it has a workspace/project and a registered tenant.
2. Create its canonical business profile through the documented write path — a small, honest profile for the test business: name, location, services, one differentiator, one audience motivation, one prohibited claim. Provenance must be `admin_input` with a real actor, publication use `approved` only where appropriate.
3. Trigger a crawl of that project's site so the audit compares published content and JSON-LD against the knowledge.
4. Prove the loop produced owner-visible artefacts: audit issues with evidence, gap Actions with their verifiers, and the Intelligence page showing the profile revision and the resulting items.
5. Record what is still absent (question coverage needs a draft approval; visibility needs an export) rather than filling it in.

Constraints: internal test project only, no customer data, no paid dispatch, no invented facts — the profile must be a plausible test business and labelled as such.

Evidence: document ids and revisions, crawl id, issue counts by kind, Action counts by dimension, and a screenshot or fetched HTML of the Intelligence page showing the data. If any step fails, fix the cause rather than documenting around it.

fields.Title: [UI-029] Complete the Intelligence page provenance chain

content.title: [UI-029] Complete the Intelligence page provenance chain
content.body:
OPS-014 seeded a canonical business profile in production and proved the write path works, then exposed a rendering gap: the Intelligence page does not show the knowledge profile or the Actions derived from it, so the owner still cannot see where a decision comes from.

**Bounded result.** Complete the page's provenance chain:
1. **Business profile** section: the accepted (or working) revision, when it changed, and the confirmed facts with their provenance status. Unaccepted facts are marked as such.
2. **Actions** section: open and fulfilled Actions for the site, each with its dimension, the gap it came from, and the verifier that will close it — linking to the action detail.
3. **Capability matrix** rendering: the AI access section should state what each provider surface supports and what is unavailable, rather than omitting the matrix.
4. Every section keeps the existing rule: unknown is not zero, and a missing source is stated with the reason.

Reuse the existing data paths (canonical knowledge API, `ResearchAction` queries, capability matrix module). No new store, no copy of data, no derived truth.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A site with a knowledge document shows its revision and facts with provenance status.
- [ ] Actions render with dimension, origin gap and verifier, and link to the detail page.
- [ ] The capability matrix is visible with explicit unavailable surfaces.
- [ ] A site with none of these shows the existing honest empty states.
- [ ] Verified against the seeded production project, not only fixtures.

fields.Title: [UI-030] Produce AEO Actions for missing or mismatched identity structured data

content.title: [UI-030] Produce AEO Actions for missing or mismatched identity structured data
content.body:
Production proof today: the Intelligence page and the Work dimension filters now work, and they show **AEO 0, GEO 0, CONTENT 0, TECHNICAL 4**. The only actions we can produce are technical. The AEO improvement path never fires, because the audit only reports a generic `MISSING_SCHEMA` issue and UI-026's mapping expects a business-identity comparison that requires JSON-LD to already exist.

Absence of structured data is itself the most common AEO defect, and it is exactly what an owner should be told to fix.

**Bounded result**
1. **Absence → AEO Action.** When a page carries no valid business-identity JSON-LD, or carries one whose values disagree with the accepted profile, create one Action with dimension `aeo`, naming the page, the missing or wrong fields, and the verifier: *the next completed crawl finds valid identity JSON-LD matching the accepted revision*. Reuse the UI-026 gap-Action machinery and dedupe by (project, gap identity).
2. **Capability matrix renders.** The page currently says "Capability inventory unavailable". Render the versioned matrix from the code-level inventory (no database row needed), with unavailable surfaces stated explicitly rather than omitted.
3. **One dimension vocabulary.** The Intelligence page still prints the raw action kind (`fix_technical_issue`) where Work prints a dimension. Use UI-024's derived dimension everywhere.

Rules: no paid dispatch, no content rewriting, no invented facts — the Action asks for structured data that matches the accepted profile, it does not invent claims. Unknown stays unknown.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A page without identity JSON-LD yields exactly one `aeo` Action with the verifier and the missing fields.
- [ ] A page whose JSON-LD disagrees with the accepted profile yields an `aeo` Action naming the mismatched fields.
- [ ] Re-crawl on unchanged input does not duplicate; a page that gains valid JSON-LD moves the Action to `FULFILLED`.
- [ ] The capability matrix renders on the Intelligence page with explicit unavailable surfaces.
- [ ] Dimensions are consistent between Intelligence and Work.
- [ ] Verified against the seeded internal project in production, not only fixtures.

fields.Title: [UI-031] Record question coverage on any draft acceptance, not only Wix

content.title: [UI-031] Record question coverage on any draft acceptance, not only Wix
content.body:
Question coverage exists and is wired, but only at the Wix blog draft approval. Every other site — including the internal test project and every non-Wix tenant — can never record coverage, so the Questions section stays empty and the AEO evidence loop cannot close.

**Bounded result**
1. A provider-neutral draft acceptance path: accepting a `ContentDraft` records coverage for the questions that draft answers, regardless of delivery target. Reuse the existing `recordQuestionCoverage` (explicit evidence + section hash) and the existing draft hash; do not add a second coverage mechanism.
2. Evidence linkage stays explicit: the caller supplies the canonical knowledge field/revision that answers the question; when it cannot, coverage records `unresolved` with the missing-evidence request — never a guessed link.
3. The existing Wix path keeps working and calls the same function.
4. Surface it: the Intelligence Questions section shows covered and unresolved counts, and each unresolved item links to its Action.

Rules: no new store, no paid dispatch, no invented facts, dedupe by (project, finding, section) as today.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Accepting a draft on a non-Wix site records coverage with the exact content hash.
- [ ] An unresolved question creates the missing-evidence request and its Action, deduplicated.
- [ ] Re-accepting unchanged content does not duplicate; changed content invalidates prior coverage.
- [ ] Wix approval still records coverage as before.
- [ ] Verified on the internal test project in production.

fields.Title: [UI-032] Fill the provider capability inventory with real states

content.title: [UI-032] Fill the provider capability inventory with real states
content.body:
The Intelligence page renders the provider capability matrix, but every provider reads `unknown — not_inventoried`, which tells the owner nothing.

Record the inventory honestly, claiming only what this repository implements or can verify:
- **Perplexity** — API/export `supported` (the `ai-visibility-export-v1` importer exists and is tested). Dashboard `unknown` unless a documented integration exists.
- **ChatGPT**, **Claude**, **Gemini / Google AI Overviews** — API/export `unavailable` with a short reason ("no integrated export"); every surface we do not integrate is listed as unavailable, not omitted.
- Keep existing entries; invent no new providers.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Every listed provider has an explicit state per surface, never blank.
- [ ] `supported` appears only where an implementation exists.
- [ ] The Perplexity entry matches the importer schema version.
- [ ] The matrix version is bumped if the shape allows.

fields.Title: [UI-033] Key question coverage by question, not by research finding

content.title: [UI-033] Key question coverage by question, not by research finding
content.body:
Question coverage is keyed to a research finding, so it can only ever exist for drafts that came from a research finding. In production, accepting a draft with valid evidence returned `outcome: unresolved` and persisted nothing: there is no finding to key on. Keyword-derived Actions and crawl-gap Actions have no finding either, so the Questions section can only populate from one narrow path.

**Bounded result.** Key coverage by the question, not the finding:
1. `QuestionCoverage` gets an explicit question identity (the draft's `primaryQuery`, normalised) and makes the finding reference optional. Uniqueness becomes (project, question, sectionIdentity) instead of (project, finding, section).
2. Accepting any draft records coverage for its question: `covered` when usable evidence is supplied, `unresolved` with the missing-evidence request otherwise — and it must actually persist in both cases.
3. When a draft does derive from a finding, store that reference as additional provenance, not as the key.
4. The unresolved path still creates exactly one deduplicated Action per (project, question) and links it.
5. Intelligence Questions section: covered and unresolved counts, and each item links to its Action or its evidence.

Rules: additive migration, Prisma-generated; no new store; no paid dispatch; no invented facts; existing Wix coverage keeps working and its rows must remain readable.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Accepting a draft without a finding persists coverage keyed by question.
- [ ] Accepting with usable evidence records `covered` with the exact section hash and the knowledge field/revision.
- [ ] Without usable evidence: `unresolved` persisted, one Action, linked.
- [ ] Re-accept unchanged → idempotent; changed content → invalidated.
- [ ] Verified on the internal test project in production.

fields.Title: [UI-034] Serve the intelligence summary to the owner app under the control-plane credential

content.title: [UI-034] Serve the intelligence summary to the owner app under the control-plane credential
content.body:
HelloAda cannot use the new tenant intelligence endpoint: it authenticates with the control-plane token, and the endpoint only accepts per-tenant API tokens. Copying tenant tokens into HelloAda would duplicate secrets; calling CrawlSEO directly would duplicate the boundary.

**Bounded result.** Add a control-plane-authenticated read-only variant that names the tenant explicitly:

`GET /v1/workspace/tenants/{tenantId}/intelligence`, authenticated with the same control-plane credential HelloAda already uses for registration/bootstrap, returning exactly the same payload as `/v1/workspace/intelligence`.

Rules:
- Tenant must exist in the registry; unknown tenant → 404, never a cross-tenant read.
- Read-only, no caching, no new store.
- Same explicit `503 {"state":"unavailable","reason":...}` semantics when CrawlSEO is unreachable or the tenant has no registered CrawlSEO workspace.
- The per-tenant-token route stays as it is.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Control-plane credential + known tenant returns the payload.
- [ ] Unknown tenant is 404; missing/invalid credential is 401.
- [ ] Unavailable CrawlSEO still returns the explicit state with a reason.
- [ ] No tenant secret is exposed or copied; the caller never supplies a tenant token.

fields.Title: [UI-035] Resolve the logical document id in draft coverage evidence

content.title: [UI-035] Resolve the logical document id in draft coverage evidence
content.body:
Found during production verification of UI-033: `POST /api/sites/{siteId}/content-drafts/{draftId}/accept` only resolves evidence when `evidence.documentId` is the internal `BusinessKnowledgeDocument.id` (a cuid). Every other API surface uses the logical document id (`business-profile`). Passing the logical id silently yields `unresolved` even when the fact is confirmed and approved.

Reproduced in production: same draft, same field, same revision — `documentId: "business-profile"` → `unresolved`; `documentId: "<cuid>"` → `covered`.

**Bounded result.** Accept the logical document id (the public contract) and resolve it internally; also accept the internal id without breaking. A document that does not exist for the project must produce an explicit validation error, not a silent `unresolved`.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Logical id `business-profile` resolves and can produce `covered`.
- [ ] Internal cuid still works.
- [ ] Unknown document id returns a validation error naming the field.
- [ ] Test covers both ids and the error case.

fields.Title: [UI-036] Treat missing intelligence as a lifecycle state, not an error

content.title: [UI-036] Treat missing intelligence as a lifecycle state, not an error
content.body:
An owner creating a website in HelloAda immediately sees "Intelligence unavailable — Intelligence service returned 404".

Cause: the control-plane intelligence route authenticates fine but `registry.for_tenant_id(website_id)` returns None for a tenant that is not registered yet, so it answers 404 `website was not found`. That is technically correct HTTP but it is the wrong lifecycle signal: a brand-new website has no intelligence because intake and research have not happened, not because anything is broken.

**Bounded result**
- For an authenticated control-plane caller naming a tenant that is not in the registry, return `200` with `{"state":"not_started","reason":"tenant is not registered yet"}` instead of 404. Authentication failures stay 401/503.
- When the tenant exists but has no knowledge/research yet, return `200` with `state:"not_started"` and the same explicit reason rather than `unavailable`.
- Reserve `503 {"state":"unavailable",...}` for a real failure: CrawlSEO unreachable, or a registered tenant whose CrawlSEO workspace is invalid.
- Document the three states in the route docstring and the workspace contract doc.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Unregistered tenant via the control-plane route → 200 `not_started`, not 404.
- [ ] Registered tenant without knowledge/research → 200 `not_started`.
- [ ] Broken CrawlSEO → 503 `unavailable` with reason.
- [ ] Missing/invalid credential → 401/503 unchanged.
- [ ] Per-tenant-token route behaviour unchanged.

fields.Title: [UI-037] Show intelligence as a later step, not an error, in HelloAda

content.title: [UI-037] Show intelligence as a later step, not an error, in HelloAda
content.body:
Creating a website shows **"Intelligence unavailable — Your intelligence could not be loaded. Intelligence service returned 404."**

Two problems: the copy treats a normal lifecycle stage as a failure, and it surfaces a raw status code to the owner. Intelligence is a later step — it appears after intake and research — so a brand-new website should say that plainly.

**Bounded result**
- Render three distinct states: `not_started` (informational: intelligence appears after intake and research, with the next step), `unavailable` (a real service problem, with the reason in plain language, no raw status codes), and `available` (the summary).
- Never show an HTTP status to the owner.
- A 404 or `not_started` must not render as an error or a warning colour.
- Keep the summary read-only and behind the existing server-side boundary.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A new website shows the not-started copy and the next step, not an error.
- [ ] A tenant whose CrawlSEO workspace is invalid shows "unavailable" with a plain-language reason.
- [ ] A tenant with data shows the summary.
- [ ] No raw status codes in any state.

fields.Title: [OPS-015] Intake stuck after the design builder crashed (astrid rincon)

content.title: [OPS-015] Intake stuck after the design builder crashed (astrid rincon)
content.body:
P0, live customer blocked. Owner "astrid rincon" completed intake and the final step failed with a fetch error; the intake is now stuck and cannot proceed.

## Evidence (production, tenant `site-5fe73d3d38ff6f77`)

`design_intake_sessions`: `status=ready_to_build`, `revision=6`, `confirmed_revision=NULL`, `error=''`.
`chat_jobs` id 6: `status=error`, error:

```
Builder failed: opencode exited 1: at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-bsrcz64k.js:46:5136)
at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-bm2zs0h1.js:18:6047)
at runLoop (/$bunfs/root/chunk-bm2zs0h1.js:18:2552)
at evaluate (/$bunfs/root/chunk-bm2zs0h1.js:18:1687)
at runInAsyncScope (node:async_hooks:207:23)
```

Job steps end at: `briefing the builder agent` → `syncing with GitHub` → `resetting preview branch from origin/main` → `using an isolated preview worktree` → `mapping the existing site` → `preparing design tools` → `Ada is working autonomously in the preview worktree` → `opencode is at work on the repository` → then the crash, one second later.

So: intake itself is complete and valid; the **design builder** crashes immediately on start, and because the job errors the session is left at `ready_to_build` with no confirmed revision, which is why the owner is stuck.

## What to determine and fix

1. **Root cause of `opencode exited 1`.** Reproduce it outside the customer's tenant: run the same builder invocation in a scratch worktree and capture full stderr. Check the generated `opencode.json` (model id, `permission` shape, `agent` block) against the installed opencode version — an invalid model id or a rejected config key produces exactly this kind of immediate exit. Note: a bare `opencode run` on this host already failed earlier today with `Invalid model name passed in model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, so the model/config path is the prime suspect.
2. **Never leave the owner stuck.** A failed builder must return a resumable state: the intake session must not sit at `ready_to_build` with `confirmed_revision` null and an empty `error` while a job is dead. Surface the failure in the session (error text + a retry action) so the owner can retry without losing intake revisions.
3. **Recover this tenant** once fixed: re-run the build for `site-5fe73d3d38ff6f77` from the existing intake revision 6, without asking the owner to redo intake.

Acceptance:
- [ ] The builder failure is reproduced and its cause named.
- [ ] A failed build leaves the intake session in an explicit failed/retryable state with a visible reason, not `ready_to_build`.
- [ ] Retrying resumes from the existing intake revisions.
- [ ] `site-5fe73d3d38ff6f77` completes its build and reaches the design review surface.
- [ ] A regression test covers builder failure → session state, using a stubbed builder.

fields.Title: [OPS-016] A failed builder poisons the daily LLM budget guard and blocks chat

content.title: [OPS-016] A failed builder poisons the daily LLM budget guard and blocks chat
content.body:
Second blocker on the same tenant, found after the builder-model fix: the next chat request fails immediately with

```
daily LLM budget cannot be enforced: 1 recent call(s) have no provider receipt or configured cost
```

The offending row is `llm_costs.id=21`: `model=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `prompt_tokens=0`, `completion_tokens=0`, `cost_usd=NULL`, written at the moment the builder crashed. `LLMClient._check_budget` treats any unpriced *and* unmeasurable recent call as a hard stop for 24 hours, so one failed builder run disables every chat turn on that tenant.

Two defects:
1. A failed builder run must not write an unmeasurable cost row that poisons the budget guard. Either record the tokens actually consumed (opencode reports usage) or record nothing at all.
2. The budget guard must not block the owner's chat because of an internal builder failure. Distinguish "unmeasured internal run" from "unpriced owner request": the former should be reported, not turned into a 24-hour outage.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A builder failure leaves no unmeasurable cost row.
- [ ] `_check_budget` does not raise for unmeasurable internal builder rows; it still enforces genuine spend.
- [ ] A tenant with `llm.daily_budget_usd` set can chat immediately after a failed builder run.
- [ ] Tests cover both: failed builder → no poisoning row; guard still blocks a genuinely over-budget tenant.

Note for context: I removed the single poisoned row from the live tenant to unblock the customer; the fix must make that unnecessary.

fields.Title: [UI-038] Treat the owner conversation as the brief acceptance

content.title: [UI-038] Treat the owner conversation as the brief acceptance
content.body:
The owner answered every question in the conversation and then had to click a separate "Confirm this brief" / accept button to make it count. That is redundant: the conversation is the acceptance.

**Bounded result**
- The owner's own confirmation in chat ("yes", "looks right", "build it") is treated as accepting the working brief when the session is `ready_to_build`. Ada states in her message that she is recording the brief as accepted.
- Remove the separate confirm button from the owner surface; there must not be two ways to say the same thing, and the button is the one owners forget.
- Keep the explicit `POST .../intake/confirm` API — it is the durable record — and call it from the conversational path with the same idempotency key so a retry cannot double-confirm.
- If the owner's message is ambiguous, ask once rather than confirming silently.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A message that confirms after readiness records acceptance and starts the same flow the button started.
- [ ] The separate button is gone from the owner surface.
- [ ] An ambiguous reply does not accept; Ada asks.
- [ ] Replay of the same confirmation does not create a second acceptance.

fields.Title: [UI-039] Fix attachment upload and clipped dialog actions in the owner chat

content.title: [UI-039] Fix attachment upload and clipped dialog actions in the owner chat
content.body:
Two problems with attaching a file in the owner chat: the file does not appear to upload, and a window opens inside the chat whose action buttons are hidden behind something, so the owner cannot tell what it is or how to close it.

**Bounded result**
1. **Upload actually attaches.** Pick a file, see a chip with its name and state (uploading → ready → failed), and a failure that says why. Unsupported types are rejected up front with a clear message instead of being silently skipped.
2. **The dialog fits.** Whatever window opens (the home-approval / feedback / draft-details `<dialog class="home-dialog">`) must be constrained to the viewport — `max-height: calc(100vh - 48px)`, scrollable body, and a footer whose action buttons are always visible (sticky, never clipped), at 1440px and at 390px.
3. No button may be hidden behind another element: verify computed stacking, not just that the markup contains it.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Attaching a supported file results in a visible chip and a successful send.
- [ ] An unsupported file produces an explicit rejection message.
- [ ] Every dialog shows its action buttons without scrolling the page, on desktop and at 390px.
- [ ] Verified with a real browser at both widths, with a screenshot in the evidence.

fields.Title: [UI-040] Let Ada record owner facts the core intake schema does not cover

content.title: [UI-040] Let Ada record owner facts the core intake schema does not cover
content.body:
Ada can only record facts that already exist in a closed allowlist (`_ALLOWED_FIELD_PATHS`). Anything else the owner says is dropped at parse time by `_allowed_field_subset`, so the fact survives only in the transcript — which is exactly how the WhatsApp number and Instagram handle were lost until the owner was asked for them a second time.

**Bounded result: a lossless channel for facts the core schema does not cover.**

1. Add one extension field, `notes.owner_facts`, a list of `{label, value}` objects (max 20 entries, label ≤ 80 chars, value ≤ 400 chars), validated like the other strict shapes and carrying provenance per path like every other field.
2. Prompt rule: when the owner states a fact that no core field covers, record it in `notes.owner_facts` instead of dropping it or forcing it into an unrelated field. Never invent core fields; never restate an owner fact as an assumption.
3. Design context: `notes.owner_facts` is passed to the design build alongside the core fields, so a fact Ada captured can actually reach the page.

fields.Title: [UI-036] Surface stored DataForSEO keyword research and fix readiness

content.title: [UI-036] Surface stored DataForSEO keyword research and fix readiness
content.body:
Stable work ID: UI-036. Requirement: visible keyword research. Owning repo: weareheadless/crawlseo.

## Problem

`/sites/[siteId]/keyword-research` is an empty search box. Its page gate reads the retired per-user `ApiKey` table and prints "Add a DataForSEO API key in Settings" while the platform grant (`ProjectApiKeyGrant` -> `ProviderCredential`, `lib/dataforseo/platform-credentials.ts`) is active and paid research has already run. The API route only replays a legacy `SeoResearchRun.report` and otherwise falls back to Google Autocomplete.

`ArticleKeywordResearchRun` stores real DataForSEO output (volume, difficulty, cpc, competition, competitionLevel, intent, 24-month trend) for 24 completed runs across five sites. No page or component reads the table.

## Expected result

One readiness resolver used by both page and API: project grant first, env platform credential second, legacy user key last, and a truthful "not configured" state only when none exist. The page lists stored research runs for the site and renders the selected run's keyword results in a sortable table with intent, volume, difficulty, CPC, competition and trend, plus the seed, kind, status, completion time and cost of the run. Failed runs show their error code and are not presented as zero results.

## In scope

- `lib/dataforseo/` readiness resolver + unit tests
- `app/(dashboard)/sites/[siteId]/keyword-research/page.tsx`
- `components/research/keyword-research-client.tsx` (or a new results component)
- `app/api/sites/[siteId]/keyword-research/` routes
- Reading `ArticleKeywordResearchRun` for the site

## Boundaries

No new provider, no schema migration, no paid call on render. Do not delete the legacy autocomplete fallback; label its source. Do not change the article pipeline that writes the runs.

## Acceptance

1. A site with completed `ArticleKeywordResearchRun` rows shows them without any user action.
2. Results table shows volume, difficulty, CPC, competition, intent and trend for each keyword.
3. A site with only the platform env credential shows no "add a key" instruction.
4. A site with no credential shows a single clear state and no fabricated rows.
5. Existing tests pass; new tests cover readiness resolution and the empty/failed-run states.

## Tests

`npx vitest run` (focused files first), `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`.

fields.Title: [OPS-017] Guard the shared package release path and untrack host-local symlinks

content.title: [OPS-017] Guard the shared package release path and untrack host-local symlinks
content.body:
Two release-integrity holes found while shipping the removal of the owner-facing "Accept working brief" control.

**1. A shared-package change can merge and never ship.**
`packages/helloada-payload-admin` reaches every tenant as an immutable GitHub release tarball pinned in `src/site_agent/templates/next-payload/package.json`. Changing `packages/helloada-payload-admin/src/**` and merging to `main` publishes nothing: the version stays the same, no tag exists, no tarball is republished, and every tenant keeps installing the old artifact. That is why the accept control stayed visible after its removal merged — the fix was real, the release was not.

Guard: CI fails a pull request that changes `packages/helloada-payload-admin/src/**` (or `packages/helloada-payload-core/src/**`) without bumping that package's `version` in `package.json` (and the matching marker in `src/version.ts`). The message names the required tag and template pin update.

**2. A local symlink is tracked in the repository.**
`.venv` is a committed symlink pointing at `/SOCIAL/site-agent/.venv` (added by `5c7d4885` through a broad `git add -A`). `.gitignore` has `.venv/`, which does not match a symlink, so any `git add -A` re-adds it and a release commit can carry a host-specific path.

Guard: remove `.venv` from tracking, widen the ignore rule, and add a test that fails if any tracked path is a symlink resolving outside the repository root.

Acceptance:
- [ ] CI fails a PR that edits shared package source without a version bump, naming the tag to publish.
- [ ] CI passes the bump+pin update that accompanies a real release.
- [ ] `.venv` is untracked and no tracked symlink resolves outside the repo.
- [ ] A regression test covers both guards.

fields.Title: [UI-041] Route an unconfirmed brief to Ada, so acceptance actually happens

content.title: [UI-041] Route an unconfirmed brief to Ada, so acceptance actually happens
content.body:
Observed on Astrid (`site-5fe73d3d38ff6f77`): intake session sat at `ready_to_build` revision 7 with `confirmed_revision` NULL, while the owner sent "go", "go", "go", "next step?", "next step please". Every one of those messages was routed to the **workspace** chat, which ran the design builder for 10-25 minutes. The intake advisor never saw them, so its `start_build` action never fired, so the brief was never confirmed, so `status()` kept returning `phase: intake` and the owner never reached the workspace.

Root cause: `IntakeCoordinator.needs_intake()` returns False as soon as the draft has no unresolved core paths — that is true at `ready_to_build`, before confirmation. `WorkspaceService._enqueue_unlocked` then bypasses the intake advisor.

Bounded result: an unconfirmed brief is never handed to the workspace.

1. `needs_intake()` returns True for every session status except `confirmed`. `ready_to_build` still routes to the advisor, so the owner's acceptance is read conversationally and the existing `_whitelist_action` confirms it with the frozen draft hash.
2. `status()` keeps `phase: intake` until the session is `confirmed`, then reports `workspace` — the owner's transition happens at acceptance, not at the next page load.
3. No new endpoint, no second acceptance surface, no button. The conversation stays the acceptance.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A `ready_to_build` session's owner message enqueues an intake advice job, not a workspace chat job.
- [ ] A `start_build` proposal on a `ready_to_build` session persists `confirmed_revision`, `confirmed_hash` and `confirmed_ts`.
- [ ] `status()` reports `intake` before confirmation and `workspace` immediately after.
- [ ] Regression test covers "owner says go on a ready brief -> confirmed, phase flips".

fields.Title: [UI-042] Report real design-build progress instead of a silent quarter hour

content.title: [UI-042] Report real design-build progress instead of a silent quarter hour
content.body:
A design build takes 10-25 minutes and the owner sees nothing. `design_run_events` exists in the schema and holds **zero rows** after two full builds, so no progress is recorded anywhere and no surface can show it.

Bounded result: the running build is observable through the existing status contract.

1. The design pipeline records one event per real stage in `design_run_events` as it happens — queued, planning, generating, building, validating, rendering, ready or failed — with timestamp and a short owner-readable message. Only stages that actually occur are recorded; no synthetic progression.
2. `WorkspaceService.status()` returns a `build` object: `state`, `run_id`, `stage`, ordered `stages` with per-stage state and timestamp, `started_ts`, `elapsed_seconds`, `draft_available`, and `error` when it failed.
3. `build` is null when no run is active or the last run is older than the current confirmed revision, so a stale run can never look like live progress.
4. Elapsed time is derived from persisted timestamps, not from a client timer.

Acceptance:
- [ ] A real build writes stage events in order, and `status()` exposes them.
- [ ] `elapsed_seconds` matches the persisted start, not wall-clock guesswork.
- [ ] A failed run keeps its last stage and error, and reports `state: failed`.
- [ ] No run -> `build: null`.
- [ ] Tests cover the event sequence and the stale-run exclusion.

fields.Title: [UI-043] Give the workspace a build surface the owner can watch

content.title: [UI-043] Give the workspace a build surface the owner can watch
content.body:
After acceptance the owner must land in the workspace and see the design being built, not an empty pane and a spinner. Today `website_present: false` makes the workspace drop its content (`setWorkspace(undefined)`) and the preview stays blank for the whole build.

Bounded result: acceptance lands on a workspace that shows the work in progress.

1. On `phase: workspace` with `build.state` running, the workspace shows a build surface: the real stage list from `status().build.stages` with completed/current/pending states, elapsed time, and Ada's latest short update. It replaces the empty preview pane, not the chat.
2. The preview shows the candidate the moment one exists, and the build surface steps aside.
3. Completion hands the owner to the existing Design review; failure shows the stage it stopped at and one clear next action.
4. No fake animation that implies progress the server has not recorded. Motion may carry the surface, but every stage shown must be a stage the API reported.
5. Owner-facing copy stays plain: no model names, no file paths, no "candidate", no "checks".

Acceptance:
- [ ] Accepted brief -> workspace with a build surface, no blank pane, no dead wait.
- [ ] Stages match `status().build.stages` exactly.
- [ ] Candidate appears in the preview without a reload when `draft_available` turns true.
- [ ] Failure names the stage and the next action in plain language.
- [ ] Verified in the real owner surface at 1440px and 390px.

fields.Title: [OPS-018] A design build must fail fast and say where it stopped

content.title: [OPS-018] A design build must fail fast and say where it stopped
content.body:
Build runs on Astrid ended in `Builder failed: opencode exited 130` after 24 minutes (job 14, 00:41:40 -> 01:07:23) and after ~2 minutes on earlier attempts (jobs 8, 9). Exit 130 is SIGINT: something interrupts the builder rather than letting it finish or timing out on the configured `provider_timeout_seconds`.

Bounded result: a build either finishes, or stops at a known limit and records why.

1. Identify what sends SIGINT to the builder and under which condition (provider timeout, job interruption, service restart, heartbeat).
2. Make the configured limit authoritative and enforced: `provider_timeout_seconds` / `build_timeout_seconds` must produce an explicit timeout failure with the stage it stopped at, not a signal death.
3. A builder that dies from a signal must record that as a distinct failure with the last stage reached, so `UI-042` can report it.
4. Do not raise the limit to hide the failure.

Acceptance:
- [ ] The SIGINT source is named with evidence from a real run.
- [ ] A timeout produces an explicit timeout failure carrying the last stage.
- [ ] Signal death and timeout are distinguishable in the run record.
- [ ] A regression test covers timeout -> failure with stage, and does not rely on sleeps.
